text: A batch job can be interrupted and restarted at any time and must cost as little as possible. Which EC2 purchasing option fits best?
explanation_en: Spot Instances offer up to 90 percent savings in exchange for the possibility of interruption with a two-minute warning, which suits fault-tolerant batch work.
tip: The words INTERRUPTIBLE, FAULT-TOLERANT, FLEXIBLE START TIME or CHEAPEST POSSIBLE always mean Spot. The two-minute interruption notice is the fact most often asked.

text: Which two statements about EC2 Savings Plans are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: They require a commitment to a consistent amount of usage measured in dollars per hour
options.B: They are purchased for 1 or 3 year terms
options.C: They guarantee capacity in a specific availability zone
options.D: They apply only to a single instance type in a single region

explanation_en: Savings Plans commit to a dollar-per-hour spend for 1 or 3 years and apply flexibly across instance families and regions. Capacity reservations are a separate feature.
tip: SAVINGS PLANS commit to SPEND ($/hour) and are flexible. RESERVED INSTANCES commit to a specific configuration. Neither guarantees capacity unless you buy a zonal RI or a capacity reservation.

text: Which service runs containers without you managing any EC2 instances?
explanation_en: Fargate is the serverless compute engine for containers, removing the need to provision or manage the underlying instances.
tip: FARGATE is the word that means 'containers without servers'. ECS and EKS are the orchestrators; each can run ON EC2 (you manage nodes) or ON FARGATE (you do not). ECR is just the image registry.

text: Which S3 storage class automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing usage patterns?
explanation_en: Intelligent-Tiering monitors access patterns and moves objects to a lower cost tier after 30 days without access, moving them back when accessed.
tip: 'UNKNOWN or CHANGING access pattern' = INTELLIGENT-TIERING (moves after 30 days). If the pattern is KNOWN and infrequent, pick Standard-IA. If it is archival, pick Glacier.

text: Which storage service provides a shared file system that many EC2 instances can mount simultaneously using NFS?
explanation_en: EFS is a managed elastic NFS file system that multiple Linux instances across availability zones can mount at the same time. A standard EBS volume attaches to one instance at a time.
tip: Storage type map: OBJECT = S3. BLOCK = EBS and instance store. FILE (shared, NFS/SMB) = EFS for Linux, FSx for Windows/Lustre. 'Multiple instances mount it at once' always means EFS or FSx.

text: Which two statements about EBS volumes are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: They persist independently of the instance lifecycle
options.B: They can be attached to an instance in a different region
options.C: They can be backed up with snapshots stored in S3
options.D: They are physically attached to the host server

explanation_en: EBS volumes persist after an instance is stopped or terminated and can be snapshotted to S3. They are network-attached and live in a single availability zone.
tip: EBS is NETWORK-attached, lives in ONE AZ, PERSISTS, snapshots to S3, and can be encrypted only at creation. Instance store is the opposite on every point except speed.

text: An application needs single-digit millisecond key-value lookups at any scale with no schema. Which database fits best?
explanation_en: DynamoDB is the managed NoSQL key-value store designed for single-digit millisecond performance at any scale.
tip: Database keyword map: KEY-VALUE / NoSQL / MILLISECOND = DynamoDB. RELATIONAL / SQL / JOINS = RDS. ANALYTICS / DATA WAREHOUSE / PETABYTES = Redshift. GRAPH / RELATIONSHIPS = Neptune. TIME SERIES = Timestream. LEDGER = QLDB.

text: Which RDS feature improves READ performance rather than availability?
explanation_en: Read replicas asynchronously copy data to additional instances that serve read traffic. Multi-AZ uses a synchronous standby that does not serve reads and exists for availability.
tip: READ REPLICA = PERFORMANCE, ASYNCHRONOUS, serves reads. MULTI-AZ = AVAILABILITY, SYNCHRONOUS, standby serves nothing. This pair is the single most tested RDS distinction.

text: Which in-memory caching engine should be chosen when the cache must survive a restart and support complex data types?
explanation_en: Redis supports persistence, replication, and complex data structures such as sorted sets used for leaderboards. Memcached is simple, multithreaded, and stores only blobs without persistence.
tip: REDIS = PERSISTS, complex types, leaderboards, session store, replication. MEMCACHED = simple blobs, multithreaded, NO persistence. If the stem mentions persistence, leaderboards or pub/sub, it is Redis.

text: Which component allows instances in a private subnet to reach the internet for updates while remaining unreachable from the internet?

options.B: An internet gateway attached to the subnet
options.D: An Elastic IP on each instance

explanation_en: A NAT gateway sits in a public subnet and allows outbound-only internet access for private subnet resources.
tip: OUTBOUND ONLY = NAT gateway (lives in a PUBLIC subnet, private subnet routes to it). A subnet becomes PUBLIC only when its route table has a default route to an INTERNET GATEWAY.

text: Which two statements about a VPC are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: A VPC spans all availability zones in a single region
options.B: A VPC can span multiple regions
options.C: A subnet exists in exactly one availability zone
options.D: A subnet can span two availability zones for redundancy

explanation_en: A VPC is regional and covers every availability zone in that region, while each subnet sits in exactly one availability zone.
tip: VPC = ONE REGION, ALL ITS AZs. SUBNET = ONE AZ. That is the entire hierarchy, and options that let a subnet span AZs or a VPC span regions are always wrong.

text: A company needs a dedicated private network connection from its datacenter to AWS with predictable latency. Which service should it use?
explanation_en: Direct Connect provides a dedicated physical link that bypasses the public internet, giving consistent bandwidth and predictable latency.
tip: DIRECT CONNECT = dedicated line, PREDICTABLE latency, not encrypted by itself, no internet access, takes weeks to provision. VPN = over the internet, encrypted, set up in minutes, variable latency.

text: Which two are valid uses of Amazon Route 53? (Choose two.)

options.B: Routing users to the endpoint with the lowest latency
options.C: Caching static content at edge locations
options.D: Terminating TLS connections for an application

explanation_en: Route 53 registers domains and provides DNS routing policies including latency-based routing. Caching is CloudFront's job and TLS termination happens at a load balancer or CloudFront.
tip: Route 53 does three things: REGISTER domains, RESOLVE DNS, and CHECK HEALTH. It never caches content and never terminates TLS - those belong to CloudFront and load balancers.

text: Which service lets you define your entire infrastructure as code in a JSON or YAML template?
explanation_en: CloudFormation is the declarative infrastructure-as-code service, using JSON or YAML templates that create and manage stacks of resources.
tip: CLOUDFORMATION = DECLARATIVE (describe the end state), templates in JSON or YAML only, resources grouped into a STACK. Systems Manager, CodeDeploy and the CLI are IMPERATIVE (step by step).

text: An Auto Scaling group has a minimum of 2, desired capacity of 4, and maximum of 8. Scaling activity has been quiet. How many instances are running?
explanation_en: Auto Scaling maintains the desired capacity, so four instances run until a scaling policy changes that number.
tip: DESIRED is what actually runs right now. MINIMUM is the floor and MAXIMUM is the ceiling. If someone terminates an instance, Auto Scaling launches one to return to DESIRED.

text: Which two ways can you interact with AWS services programmatically? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: The CLI and the SDKs both call the AWS APIs programmatically. The console is a graphical interface and Artifact is a document portal.
tip: Three access methods: CONSOLE (browser), CLI (terminal), SDK (code in a language). All three ultimately call the same APIs over HTTPS on port 443.

text: Which CloudWatch component stores the text output written by an application?
explanation_en: CloudWatch Logs ingests and stores log data, with retention configurable from one day to ten years.
tip: METRICS = numbers (kept 15 months). LOGS = text (retention 1 day to 10 years). ALARMS = thresholds on metrics. DASHBOARDS = visualization. Match the data type in the stem.

text: Which decoupling service delivers messages to a queue where they are processed once by a single consumer?
explanation_en: SQS is a message queue where each message is retrieved and processed by one consumer. SNS is publish-subscribe and fans a message out to many subscribers.
tip: SQS = QUEUE, pull, one consumer per message, decouples components. SNS = PUB/SUB, push, fans out to many subscribers. 'Queue' versus 'notify everyone' is the discriminator.

text: Which service coordinates multiple AWS services into a visual workflow with steps, branches, and retries?
explanation_en: Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows as state machines with built-in error handling and retry logic.
tip: The words WORKFLOW, ORCHESTRATE, STATE MACHINE or MULTI-STEP WITH RETRIES point to Step Functions. Lambda runs one function; Step Functions chains many together.

text: A developer wants to upload application code and have AWS provision and manage the infrastructure automatically. Which service fits?
explanation_en: Elastic Beanstalk takes uploaded code and handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring automatically. You pay only for the underlying resources.
tip: 'JUST UPLOAD MY CODE' = ELASTIC BEANSTALK (free service, you pay for the EC2/ELB underneath). Lightsail is a fixed-price preconfigured server; CloudFormation builds infrastructure, not applications.

text: Which two S3 features help control storage cost over an object's lifetime? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: Lifecycle configurations do exactly two things: transition objects to cheaper storage classes and expire (delete) them. Replication increases cost and bucket policies control access.
tip: Lifecycle = TRANSITION (move to cheaper class) + EXPIRATION (delete). Nothing else. If an option mentions encrypting, compressing or replicating, it is not a lifecycle action.

text: What is the maximum size of a single object stored in Amazon S3?
explanation_en: A single S3 object can be up to 5 TB. Uploads larger than 5 GB must use multipart upload.
tip: Numbers worth memorizing: S3 object max 5 TB, single PUT max 5 GB (above that use multipart), key up to 1,024 bytes, bucket name 3 to 63 characters. Glacier archives go up to 40 TB.

text: Which two database engines are supported by Amazon RDS? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: RDS supports MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, and Aurora. MongoDB and Cassandra are non-relational and served by DocumentDB and Keyspaces respectively.
tip: Six RDS engines only: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, Aurora. MongoDB-compatible = DocumentDB. Cassandra-compatible = Keyspaces. Neither is an RDS engine.

text: Which two statements about CloudFront are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: It caches content at edge locations close to users
options.B: It can serve content from an S3 bucket or an EC2 origin
options.C: It stores the only copy of your content
options.D: It replaces the need for a load balancer

explanation_en: CloudFront caches copies of content at edge locations and can pull from S3 buckets, load balancers, EC2 instances, or any custom HTTP origin. The origin always keeps the authoritative copy.
tip: ORIGIN keeps the real copy, EDGE LOCATION keeps the cached copy, DISTRIBUTION is the configuration. CloudFront never replaces an origin or a load balancer - it sits in front of them.

text: Which two are true about Amazon Lightsail? (Choose two.)

options.A: It bills at a predictable flat monthly rate
options.C: It provides fine-grained control over VPC networking
options.D: It is billed per second like EC2

explanation_en: Lightsail bundles compute, storage, and networking at a fixed monthly price and offers blueprints such as WordPress and LAMP. It deliberately hides advanced networking configuration.
tip: LIGHTSAIL = FLAT RATE ($3.50 to $160/month) + BLUEPRINTS + simplicity, running on EC2 underneath. If the stem wants fine-grained control, the answer moves to EC2.

text: Which service provides a managed way to run scheduled or event-driven operational tasks across a fleet of EC2 instances?
explanation_en: Systems Manager provides Run Command, Automation documents, Patch Manager, and Session Manager to operate fleets of instances.
tip: SYSTEMS MANAGER = operate the fleet you already have (run scripts, patch, connect without SSH). COMMAND documents run scripts ON the instance; AUTOMATION documents perform AWS API tasks.

text: A company must transfer 500 TB from its datacenter to AWS where the network link would take months. What should it use?

options.C: AWS DataSync over the existing link

explanation_en: Snowball Edge devices, which can be clustered, are the right scale for hundreds of terabytes. Snowmobile is intended for exabyte-scale transfers.
tip: Scale ladder: SNOWCONE 8-14 TB (up to 22 TB SSD) > SNOWBALL / SNOWBALL EDGE tens of TB each, clusterable > SNOWMOBILE up to 100 PB in a truck. Hundreds of TB = Snowball, petabytes+ = Snowmobile.

text: Which two statements about a newly created security group are correct? (Choose two.)

options.D: It contains a default deny rule for outbound traffic

explanation_en: A new security group starts with zero inbound rules, blocking all incoming traffic, and one outbound rule allowing all traffic to any destination.
tip: New security group: INBOUND EMPTY (so nothing gets in), OUTBOUND ALLOW ALL. And remember security groups have no deny rules at all - only NACLs do.

text: Which service is purpose-built for petabyte-scale data warehousing and complex analytical queries?
explanation_en: Redshift is the columnar data warehouse designed for large-scale analytics, scaling from 1 to 128 nodes.
tip: DATA WAREHOUSE, BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE, PETABYTES or COMPLEX REPORTING = Redshift. Add SPECTRUM if the data stays in S3. Transactional workloads go to RDS or DynamoDB instead.

text: Which two statements about resource tags are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: Tag keys and values are case-sensitive
options.D: A resource can have unlimited tags

explanation_en: Tags require a key, allow an optional value, are case-sensitive, and are limited to 50 per resource.
tip: Tag rules: KEY MANDATORY, VALUE OPTIONAL, CASE-SENSITIVE, MAX 50 per resource. Tags are also the mechanism behind cost allocation reports.

text: Which two are true about a launch template compared to a launch configuration? (Choose two.)

options.B: A launch template can be used for manual instance launches
options.C: A launch configuration can be modified after creation

explanation_en: Launch templates are versioned and can be used both by Auto Scaling and for manual launches. Launch configurations are immutable and work only with Auto Scaling.
tip: LAUNCH TEMPLATE = versioned, modifiable, works manually AND with Auto Scaling (AWS recommends it). LAUNCH CONFIGURATION = immutable, Auto Scaling only, legacy.

text: Which EC2 instance family should be chosen for an in-memory database with very high RAM requirements?
explanation_en: Memory optimized instances provide a high ratio of RAM to vCPU, which suits in-memory databases and large caches.
tip: Family by bottleneck: GENERAL PURPOSE = balanced. COMPUTE OPTIMIZED = CPU-heavy (batch, gaming servers). MEMORY OPTIMIZED = RAM-heavy (in-memory DBs). STORAGE OPTIMIZED = high disk IOPS. ACCELERATED = GPU/ML.

text: Which Route 53 routing policy sends users to the region that gives them the fastest response time?
explanation_en: Latency-based routing measures the network latency between the user and each region and returns the fastest one. Geolocation routes on the user's location rather than measured performance.
tip: FASTEST RESPONSE = Latency. USER'S COUNTRY (for legal or language reasons) = Geolocation. PERCENTAGE SPLIT / A-B TESTING = Weighted. ACTIVE-PASSIVE = Failover. RANDOM ORDER = Multivalue Answer.

text: Which service should be used to trigger a Lambda function every day at 6:00 AM?

options.A: Amazon EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) with a scheduled rule
options.B: A CloudWatch alarm on CPU utilization

explanation_en: EventBridge, formerly CloudWatch Events, supports schedule expressions that invoke targets such as Lambda at a fixed time or interval.
tip: A SCHEDULE or a SPECIFIC API ACTION = EventBridge / CloudWatch Events. A METRIC CROSSING A THRESHOLD = CloudWatch Alarm. The words 'at a specific time' rule out alarms entirely.

text: Which two statements about S3 durability and availability are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: S3 Standard is designed for eleven nines of durability
options.B: S3 One Zone-IA has lower availability than S3 Standard
options.C: Durability and availability mean the same thing

explanation_en: S3 Standard offers 99.999999999 percent durability and 99.99 percent availability, while One Zone-IA drops availability to 99.5 percent because the data sits in a single availability zone. No service offers 100 percent availability.
tip: DURABILITY = data is not lost (eleven nines on every class except RRS). AVAILABILITY = you can reach it right now (Standard 99.99%, Standard-IA 99.9%, One Zone-IA 99.5% - the lowest). Never confuse the two.
